claims.text: Evil is structurally parasitic on prior good — every evil act is defined by the good it violates.
claims.reviewer_notes: Core structural claim; well-supported by theological tradition and logical analysis.

claims.text: Information theory proves that a deceptive ground state maximizes entropy — producing noise, not structure.
claims.reviewer_notes: Analogically strong but requires careful mapping from communication channels to metaphysical foundations.

claims.text: The Byzantine Generals Problem demonstrates that coordinated systems require honest signals — the physical constants coordinate with precision beyond probability, proving the ground signal is clean.
claims.reviewer_notes: Strong analogy; depends on the assumption that physical constants are signals from a common source.

claims.text: The 'Evil-God Challenge' (Stephen Law) breaks on asymmetry — an evil God needs creation (incomplete), must violate a prior standard of good (subordinate), and cannot explain oxytocin, self-sacrifice, music, or E=mc².
claims.reviewer_notes: Well-reasoned refutation; the asymmetry arguments are logically sound and empirically grounded.

claims.text: Truth and love are the same thing at the bottom — a truthful ground that creates freely and gives generously is what love looks like when it takes structural form.
claims.reviewer_notes: Poetic and evocative but not directly argued or evidenced in the source; speculative synthesis.
